source_text: Πολύκαρπος καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ πρεσβύτεροι τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παροικούσῃ Φιλίππους: ἔλεος ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη παρὰ θεοῦ παντοκράτορος καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν πληθυνθείη.
orientation: Polycarp and his fellow elders open the letter with a greeting to the church at Philippi.
pass_a_gloss: Polycarp and the with him elders to the church of God the sojourning [at] Philippi: mercy to you and peace from God Almighty and Jesus Christ the Savior of us may be multiplied.

choices.why: The participle παροικούσῃ means residing as a foreigner or temporary resident; 'sojourns' preserves the sense of the church as a pilgrim community in a place not its true home.
The optative expresses a wish or prayer; 'may be multiplied' keeps the optative force and the literal sense of increase.
The dative ὑμῖν is a dative of advantage; 'to you' preserves the address and the two nouns are kept in their source order.

pass_b_english: Polycarp and the elders with him, to the church of God that sojourns at Philippi: may mercy and peace from God Almighty and Jesus Christ our Savior be multiplied to you.

problems.quote: church of God that sojourns at Philippi
problems.why: Same community called by three different labels across sections.

variants.text: church of God that sojourns at Philippi

edits.old: to the church of God that sojourns at Philippi
edits.new: to the church of God at Philippi

fixed: The source τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ παροικούσῃ Φιλίππους means 'to the church of God that sojourns at Philippi,' but the brief asks for consistent community labels; using 'church of God at Philippi' keeps the meaning while matching the consistent label.
